questions.question: Which of the following trace elements is essential for the formation of haemoglobin in the human body? (a) zinc (b) copper (c) iron (d) iodine
questions.solution:
Haemoglobin is an iron-containing protein; each of its four haem groups has an $Fe^{2+}$ ion at the centre of a porphyrin ring, and this iron reversibly binds oxygen. Iron is therefore the essential trace element for haemoglobin formation.

Other micro-nutrients have different roles: **zinc** is needed for enzyme activity and growth, **copper** for iron utilisation and connective tissue, and **iodine** for the hormone thyroxine.

**Answer: (c) iron**

A deficiency of iron lowers the haemoglobin content of the blood, producing anaemia, for which iron-rich foods or ferrous sulphate tablets are prescribed.
questions.knowledgeNote: Iron is the central constituent of the haem group of haemoglobin; its deficiency causes anaemia.
